title: Independence Proclaimed — Houphouët-Boigny Becomes First President
note: Independence declared August 7, 1960; Houphouet-Boigny elected president November 27, 1960. Core claim confirmed.

title: Single-Party Constitutional Framework Established
note: PDCI single-party rule and strong presidential constitution established at independence. Well-documented.

title: Franco-Ivorian Defense Agreements Entrench Françafrique
note: Defense cooperation agreements signed in 1961 keeping French military presence. Confirmed by multiple sources.

title: Caisse de Stabilisation (CAISTAB) Established for Cocoa and Coffee
note: CAISTAB establishment in early 1960s as cocoa/coffee marketing board is well-documented in economic histories of Ivory Coast.

title: Ivory Coast Surpasses 300,000 Tonnes of Cocoa Production
note: Production grew 6-7% per year 1965-74 from ~60,000t at independence; 300,000t by 1965 is implausible given the growth trajectory. The milestone likely occurred later (early 1970s). Specific 1965 figure unconfirmed.

title: Gagnoa Uprising Suppressed with Significant Casualties
note: Bete uprising under Kragbé Gnagbé in Gagnoa region October 1970, suppressed by army. Casualties contested (71 confirmed, 4000 rumored). Core event confirmed.

title: Oil Shock Hits Import-Dependent Economy
note: 1973 OPEC oil embargo impacted Ivory Coast as an oil-importing country. General impact is accurate and well-documented.

title: Kossou Dam Displacement Crisis Affects 75,000 Baoulé
note: Year is wrong. The Kossou Dam was built 1969-1972 and completed in 1973. Displacement of ~75,000 Baoulé occurred during construction, not 1975.

title: Ivory Coast Becomes World's Top Cocoa Producer
note: Year is wrong. Ivory Coast overtook Ghana as world's top cocoa producer in 1978, not 1976.

title: Debt-Financed Spending Surges as Commodity Revenues Soften
note: Late-1970s debt-financed spending surge as commodity prices softened is well-documented in Ivory Coast economic histories.

title: Cocoa Price Collapse Ends 'Ivorian Miracle' Growth
note: Cocoa price collapse from late-1970s peaks and beginning of economic decline around 1980 is well-documented.

title: Debt Crisis and Paris Club Rescheduling
note: Ivory Coast entered debt crisis and Paris Club rescheduling in the early 1980s. Core claim confirmed.

title: Yamoussoukro Designated Official Capital
note: Yamoussoukro designated political capital on March 21, 1983. Basilica cornerstone laid 1985, consecrated 1990 — not 'nearly complete' in 1983 as stated. Minor inaccuracy in description but year and core designation confirmed.

title: IMF Structural Adjustment Agreement Imposes Austerity
note: IMF structural adjustment programs in Ivory Coast in the mid-1980s are well-documented.

title: Deforestation Destroys Over 75 Percent of Original Forest Cover
note: Massive deforestation by the 1980s from 16M to ~4M hectares is confirmed in environmental literature.

title: Student Protests Escalate — FESCI Radicalized
note: FESCI student protests and radicalization in late 1980s is documented. Year approximate but consistent with sources.

title: Multi-Party Democracy Legalized After Three Decades of Single-Party Rule
note: Opposition parties legalized May 3, 1990. FPI registered and ran in first multiparty elections. Confirmed.

title: Alassane Ouattara Appointed Prime Minister to Manage Austerity
note: Ouattara appointed PM by Houphouet-Boigny in 1990 to implement economic stabilization. Confirmed.

title: Soldiers Beat Students at Yamoussoukro — Military Accountability Tested
note: 1991 military barracks beating of students and subsequent trial of the general responsible is confirmed in human rights records.

title: Houphouët-Boigny Dies After 33 Years in Power
note: Houphouet-Boigny died December 7, 1993. Bedie (National Assembly Speaker, not explicitly titled 'Speaker' — he was President of the National Assembly) succeeded him constitutionally. Confirmed.

title: CFA Franc Devaluation Triggers Economic Shock
note: 50% CFA franc devaluation January 12, 1994. Impact on Ivory Coast confirmed across multiple sources.

title: Ivoirité Doctrine Emerges — Ouattara's Eligibility Contested
note: Ivoirité concept and electoral code amendment (December 1994) explicitly targeting Ouattara's eligibility confirmed. Year is accurate.

title: Land Tenure Conflicts Erupt in Forest Zones
note: Escalating land conflicts in southwestern forest zones mid-to-late 1990s between autochthonous and migrant communities is documented.

title: New Land Law Restricts Ownership to Citizens, Threatening Migrant Farmers
note: 1998 land law restricting rural land ownership to Ivorian citizens confirmed in multiple sources.

title: Military Coup Overthrows Bédié — First Coup in Ivorian History
note: December 24, 1999 coup by General Guei confirmed as first coup in Ivorian history. All details accurate.

title: Laurent Gbagbo Wins Disputed Presidential Election
note: October 2000 election: Guei tried to steal result, mass protests ousted him, Gbagbo declared winner. Ouattara excluded under ivoirité. Confirmed.

title: Post-Election Violence Claims Dozens of Lives — Impunity Established
note: Post-election violence and killings of RDR supporters in Abidjan forests confirmed by Human Rights Watch.

title: National Reconciliation Forum Fails to Resolve Core Disputes
note: 2001 national reconciliation forum including Bedie and Ouattara documented; failure to implement agreements is consistent with historical record.

title: September 19 Rebellion — Civil War Begins, Country Divided
note: September 19, 2002 military uprising seizing Bouaké and northern regions confirmed. French buffer zone established. All details accurate.

title: Forces Nouvelles Unified Rebel Coalition Controls North
note: Forces Nouvelles merger of rebel factions in December 2002 under Soro confirmed. Controlled northern Ivory Coast from Bouaké.

title: Linas-Marcoussis Peace Agreement Signed Under French Pressure
note: January 15-24, 2003 peace talks near Paris producing Linas-Marcoussis Agreement confirmed. Pro-Gbagbo protests against French imposition documented.

title: Human Rights Abuses Documented by Both Sides
note: HRW and Amnesty documentation of abuses by both sides confirmed.

title: Ivory Coast Air Strikes Kill Nine French Soldiers — Crisis with France
note: November 6, 2004 Bouaké attack: 9 French soldiers killed, 1 US civilian killed. France destroyed Ivorian Air Force. All core facts confirmed.

title: UN ONUCI Peacekeeping Mission Deployed
note: UNOCI established April 4, 2004 per Security Council resolution 1528 of February 27, 2004. Confirmed.

title: Probo Koala Toxic Waste Disaster Kills 16 in Abidjan
note: Death toll is wrong. Confirmed deaths: 17 (not 16), with at least 30,000 injured. The number stated (16) is incorrect; the actual confirmed figure is 17.

title: Ouagadougou Political Agreement Opens Path to Elections
note: March 4, 2007 agreement between Gbagbo and Soro confirmed. Soro appointed PM March 29, 2007. All details accurate.

title: Presidential Runoff — Disputed Results Trigger Constitutional Crisis
note: November 28, 2010 runoff; IEC certified Ouattara ~54%; Constitutional Council declared Gbagbo winner; both inaugurated. All details confirmed.

title: Second Civil War — Post-Election Conflict Kills Thousands
note: December 2010 to April 2011 conflict with thousands killed, Duékoué massacres, FRCI advance confirmed.

title: Gbagbo Arrested — Ouattara Assumes Undisputed Presidency
note: April 11, 2011 capture with French military support confirmed. Gbagbo transferred to ICC November 2011. All details accurate.

title: Duékoué Massacre — Pro-Ouattara Forces Kill Hundreds of Civilians
note: March 29, 2011 Duékoué massacre by FRCI forces confirmed; Guéré victims; ICRC estimated 800+ dead. Confirmed.

title: Post-Conflict Reconstruction Drives 9 Percent GDP Growth
note: Strong post-conflict GDP rebound (~9%) in 2012 confirmed by World Bank and IMF reports.

title: Truth, Dialogue, and Reconciliation Commission Established
note: CDVR established under Charles Konan Banny confirmed. Criticisms about selective accountability also documented.

title: ICC Trial of Laurent Gbagbo Begins
note: ICC proceedings against Gbagbo for crimes against humanity confirmed. Formal trial began in 2016; confirmation of charges hearing in 2013. Core claim accurate.

title: Cocoa Sector Reform Guarantees Farmers 60 Percent of World Price
note: Conseil Café Cacao established; 60% farmgate price guarantee policy confirmed.

title: Ouattara Re-elected in Peaceful Election — Democratic Consolidation Milestone
note: October 25, 2015 election: Ouattara won 83.66%. Described as peaceful; some opposition boycott. All details confirmed.

title: New Constitution Establishes Third Republic
note: October 30, 2016 referendum; 93.42% yes, 42.42% turnout. Senate and vice presidency created. All details confirmed.

title: Cocoa Price Crash of 30 Percent Damages Farmer Incomes
note: ~30% cocoa price fall in 2017 documented; impact on Ivory Coast farmers confirmed across commodity market sources.

title: Military Mutiny — Ex-Combatants Demand Bonus Payments
note: January and May 2017 mutinies by ex-Forces Nouvelles fighters confirmed. Bonus payments agreed. Event description accurate; payment amount stated (12M CFA) differs slightly from sources (5M + 7M = 12M CFA staggered) — correct total.

title: Gbagbo Acquitted by ICC — Prosecution Finds Insufficient Evidence
note: January 15, 2019 acquittal on all crimes against humanity charges confirmed. Upheld on appeal March 31, 2021.

title: Ouattara Seeks Third Term After PM Gon Coulibaly Dies — Constitutional Controversy
note: Gon Coulibaly died July 2020; Ouattara reversed retirement; opposition boycotted; violence killed ~85 people (sources say ~50+ killed). Core claim confirmed.

title: Gbagbo Returns to Ivory Coast After a Decade Abroad
note: Gbagbo returned June 17, 2021. Founded PPA-CI (African People's Party – Côte d'Ivoire) in October 2021. All details confirmed.

title: 49 Ivorian Soldiers Detained by Mali Junta — Regional Diplomatic Crisis
note: 49 soldiers arrested July 2022 in Bamako; pardoned and released January 6-7, 2023. ECOWAS/Togolese mediation confirmed.

title: Henri Konan Bédié Dies — Last Figure of Post-Houphouët Triumvirate Gone
note: Bédié died August 1, 2023 aged 89. All details confirmed.

title: Ivory Coast Hosts and Wins AFCON 2024 — Historic National Triumph
note: Ivory Coast beat Nigeria 2-1 in final (February 11, 2024) at Ebimpé. Emerse Faé took over mid-tournament. All details confirmed.

title: Cocoa Prices Hit Historic High Above $10,000 Per Tonne
note: Cocoa surpassed $10,000/tonne in March 2024; reached $12,646 by December 2024. El Niño crop failures confirmed as driver.

title: EU Deforestation Regulation Forces Cocoa Supply Chain Overhaul
note: EUDR requiring deforestation-free cocoa supply chains and its impact on Ivory Coast is confirmed. Satellite monitoring and certification programs documented.

title: Presidential Election — Most Competitive Since Crisis Years Anticipated
note: October 2025 presidential election held; Ouattara won a fourth term. Election was contested with opposition participation. Core claim confirmed.
